sections.title: The Earthly Sanctuary and Its Limitations
observations: The chapter begins by describing the earthly sanctuary, which was a shadow of the heavenly realities. The tabernacle and its furnishings were designed according to God's instructions, serving as a place for worship and sacrifice.

The limitations of the earthly sanctuary are highlighted, particularly that it could not provide true cleansing from sin. The rituals performed there were temporary and pointed to a greater reality that was to come.

sections.title: The Superior Ministry of Christ
observations: In contrast to the earthly priests, Christ entered the heavenly sanctuary, not made with human hands. His ministry is superior because He offers Himself as the perfect sacrifice, once for all, securing eternal redemption for believers.
The blood of Christ is emphasized as being far more effective than the blood of animals, as it cleanses the conscience and allows believers to serve the living God.

sections.title: The New Covenant and Its Implications
observations: The chapter concludes with a discussion of the new covenant established by Christ's sacrifice. This covenant is based on better promises and provides a means for true forgiveness and relationship with God.

The necessity of Christ's death is underscored, as a will is only effective upon the death of the one who made it. This illustrates the importance of Christ's sacrificial death in bringing about the new covenant.

importantVerses.commentary: He entered once for all into the holy places, not by means of the blood of goats and calves but by means of his own blood, thus securing an eternal redemption for us.
Indeed, under the law almost everything is purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness of sins.

questions: What does the comparison between the earthly sanctuary and the heavenly sanctuary teach us about the nature of Christ's sacrifice?
How does the concept of the new covenant change our understanding of our relationship with God?
In what ways does the shedding of Christ's blood fulfill the requirements of the law regarding forgiveness?
